DAN.P.4.4-18.text: Nebuchadnezzar’s Dream of a Great Tree

DAN.P.7.1-8.text: Daniel’s Vision of the Four Beasts

DAN.P.7.9-12.text: Daniel’s Vision of the Ancient of Days

DAN.P.7.13-14.text: Daniel’s Vision of the Son of Man

DAN.P.8.1-14.text: Daniel’s Vision of the Ram and the Goat

DAN.P.9.20-27.text: Gabriel’s Prophecy of the Seventy Weeks

DAN.P.11.1-35.text: Kings of the South and North

DAN.1.1-2.text: Nebuchadnezzar takes Jehoiakim and temple items to Babylon

DAN.1.3-5.text: The king orders young Israelites trained for service

DAN.1.6-7.text: Daniel and three friends receive new Babylonian names

DAN.1.8-10.text: Daniel asks not to eat the king’s food

DAN.1.11-13.text: Daniel asks the steward for a ten-day test

DAN.1.14-16.text: After ten days, Daniel and his friends look healthier

DAN.1.17-18.text: God gives the four young men wisdom and understanding

DAN.1.19-21.text: The king finds the four young men wiser than all others

DAN.2.1-2.text: Nebuchadnezzar has troubling dreams and calls his wise men

DAN.2.3-4.text: The astrologers ask the king to tell his dream

DAN.2.5-6.text: The king demands the dream and its meaning, or death

DAN.2.7-9.text: The king says the astrologers are stalling for time

DAN.2.10-11.text: The astrologers say no one can tell the king’s dream

DAN.2.12-13.text: The king orders all the wise men of Babylon killed

DAN.2.14-16.text: Daniel asks the king for time to explain the dream

DAN.2.17-18.text: Daniel asks his friends to pray for mercy from God

DAN.2.19-20.text: God shows Daniel the mystery, and Daniel praises God

DAN.2.21-22.text: Daniel says God changes times and reveals hidden things

DAN.2.23-23.text: Daniel thanks God for showing the king’s dream

DAN.2.24-24.text: Daniel asks Arioch not to kill the wise men

DAN.2.25-26.text: Arioch brings Daniel to the king

DAN.2.27-28.text: Daniel says only God in heaven reveals mysteries

DAN.2.29-30.text: Daniel says God has revealed the mystery to him

DAN.2.31-33.text: Daniel describes the king’s dream of a great statue

DAN.2.34-35.text: A stone destroys the statue and fills the earth

DAN.2.36-38.text: Daniel tells Nebuchadnezzar he is the head of gold

DAN.2.39-39.text: Two more kingdoms will rule after Nebuchadnezzar

DAN.2.40-40.text: A fourth kingdom will be strong like iron

DAN.2.41-43.text: The fourth kingdom will be divided and partly brittle

DAN.2.44-45.text: God will set up a kingdom that never ends

DAN.2.46-47.text: Nebuchadnezzar honors Daniel and praises Daniel’s God

DAN.2.48-49.text: The king gives Daniel and his friends high positions

DAN.3.1-2.text: Nebuchadnezzar builds a golden statue and calls officials

DAN.3.3-5.text: The herald commands all people to worship the statue

DAN.3.6-7.text: The people worship the statue to avoid the furnace

DAN.3.8-10.text: Astrologers remind the king of his order to worship

DAN.3.11-12.text: Astrologers say three Jews refuse to worship the statue

DAN.3.13-14.text: Nebuchadnezzar angrily questions the three Jews

DAN.3.15-15.text: Nebuchadnezzar threatens the three Jews with the furnace

DAN.3.16-18.text: The three men refuse to serve the king’s gods

DAN.3.19-20.text: Angry king orders the three men thrown into a hot furnace

DAN.3.21-23.text: Soldiers die as the three bound men fall into the fire

DAN.3.24-25.text: Nebuchadnezzar sees four men walking unharmed in the fire

DAN.3.26-27.text: The three men come out of the fire without harm

DAN.3.28-28.text: Nebuchadnezzar praises the God who saved his servants

DAN.3.29-30.text: The king orders respect for God and promotes the three men

DAN.4.4-6.text: Nebuchadnezzar has a frightening dream and calls wise men

DAN.4.7-9.text: Nebuchadnezzar asks Daniel to explain the dream

DAN.4.10-12.text: Nebuchadnezzar sees a huge tree that feeds all creatures

DAN.4.13-14.text: A holy watcher from heaven orders the tree cut down

DAN.4.15-16.text: The stump stays while a man lives like a beast

DAN.4.17-18.text: God rules all kingdoms; the king asks Daniel for meaning

DAN.4.19-19.text: Daniel is troubled, and the king comforts him

DAN.4.20-22.text: Daniel says the king is the great tree

DAN.4.23-23.text: Daniel repeats the watcher’s order to cut down the tree

DAN.4.24-25.text: Daniel says the king will live with the beasts

DAN.4.26-27.text: Daniel urges the king to turn from sin and show mercy

DAN.4.28-30.text: Nebuchadnezzar boasts about the Babylon he built

DAN.4.31-32.text: A voice from heaven says the king will lose his kingdom

DAN.4.33-33.text: Nebuchadnezzar is driven out and lives like an animal

DAN.4.34-34.text: Nebuchadnezzar regains his mind and praises the Most High

DAN.4.35-35.text: Nebuchadnezzar says God rules and no one can stop him

DAN.4.36-37.text: Nebuchadnezzar gets his throne back and praises God

DAN.5.1-2.text: Belshazzar uses the temple vessels at his feast

DAN.5.3-4.text: The king and guests drink wine and praise gods

DAN.5.5-6.text: A hand writes on the wall and the king is terrified

DAN.5.7-7.text: The king offers rewards to anyone who explains the writing

DAN.5.8-9.text: The wise men cannot read the writing, so fear grows

DAN.5.10-10.text: The queen comes in and tells the king not to be afraid

DAN.5.11-12.text: The queen tells the king to call Daniel to explain

DAN.5.13-14.text: Belshazzar speaks to Daniel about his wisdom

DAN.5.15-16.text: Belshazzar offers Daniel rewards to read the writing

DAN.5.17-19.text: Daniel refuses gifts and speaks of Nebuchadnezzar’s power

DAN.5.20-21.text: Nebuchadnezzar became proud and lived like a wild animal

DAN.5.22-24.text: Daniel tells Belshazzar he did not honor God

DAN.5.25-28.text: Daniel says God has ended Belshazzar’s reign

DAN.5.29-31.text: Daniel is honored and Belshazzar dies that night

DAN.6.1-3.text: Darius appoints rulers and Daniel stands out

DAN.6.4-5.text: Officials try to accuse Daniel but find no fault

DAN.6.6-7.text: Officials ask Darius to forbid prayer to any god but him

DAN.6.8-9.text: Darius signs the decree that cannot be changed

DAN.6.10-11.text: Daniel keeps praying to God and officials find him

DAN.6.12-12.text: Officials remind Darius of his decree

DAN.6.13-14.text: Officials accuse Daniel and Darius tries to save him

DAN.6.15-15.text: Officials tell Darius the law cannot be changed

DAN.6.16-16.text: Darius has Daniel thrown to the lions

DAN.6.17-18.text: Daniel’s den is sealed and Darius cannot sleep

DAN.6.19-20.text: Darius hurries to the den and calls to Daniel

DAN.6.21-22.text: Daniel says God shut the mouths of the lions

DAN.6.23-23.text: Daniel is lifted out without any wounds

DAN.6.24-24.text: Daniel’s accusers are thrown to the lions

DAN.6.25-25.text: Darius writes a letter to all the nations

DAN.6.26-27.text: Darius orders people to fear the God of Daniel

DAN.6.28-28.text: Daniel prospers under Darius and Cyrus

DAN.7.1-3.text: Daniel dreams of four beasts from the sea

DAN.7.4-5.text: Daniel sees a lion-like beast and a bear-like beast

DAN.7.6-7.text: Daniel sees a leopard-like beast and a terrible beast

DAN.7.8-8.text: Daniel sees a little horn that speaks proudly

DAN.7.9-9.text: Daniel sees the Ancient of Days take his seat

DAN.7.10-10.text: Daniel sees God’s court meet and the books opened

DAN.7.11-12.text: Daniel sees the beast destroyed in the fire

DAN.7.13-14.text: Daniel’s Vision of the Son of Man

DAN.7.15-16.text: Daniel is afraid and asks what the visions mean

DAN.7.17-18.text: Four kings will rise, but God’s people get the kingdom

DAN.7.19-20.text: Daniel asks about the fourth beast and the horns

DAN.7.21-22.text: The horn fights God’s people until God judges

DAN.7.23-24.text: The fourth beast is a kingdom with ten kings

DAN.7.25-26.text: A king will oppress God’s people, but God will judge him

DAN.7.27-28.text: God’s people receive the kingdom; Daniel is troubled

DAN.8.1-2.text: Daniel sees himself in Susa beside the Ulai Canal

DAN.8.3-4.text: Daniel sees a powerful ram with two horns

DAN.8.5-6.text: A goat with one horn rushes at the ram

DAN.8.7-8.text: The goat destroys the ram, then its large horn breaks

DAN.8.9-10.text: A little horn grows and attacks the host of heaven

DAN.8.11-12.text: The little horn opposes the Prince and removes sacrifice

DAN.8.13-14.text: A holy one says the sanctuary will be restored

DAN.8.15-17.text: Gabriel comes to explain the vision to Daniel

DAN.8.18-19.text: Gabriel helps Daniel stand and speaks of the end time

DAN.8.20-21.text: The ram is Media and Persia; the goat is Greece

DAN.8.22-23.text: Four kingdoms come, then a proud king rises

DAN.8.24-25.text: A strong king will destroy many but will be broken

DAN.8.26-26.text: Gabriel tells Daniel to seal up the vision

DAN.8.27-27.text: Daniel is ill and does not understand the vision

DAN.9.1-2.text: Daniel learns how long Jerusalem will be desolate

DAN.9.3-4.text: Daniel begins to pray to God with fasting

DAN.9.5-6.text: Daniel confesses that Israel has sinned and rebelled

DAN.9.7-8.text: Daniel says Israel is covered with shame for sin

DAN.9.9-11.text: Daniel says God is merciful, but Israel broke his law

DAN.9.12-14.text: Daniel says God was right to bring disaster on Israel

DAN.9.15-16.text: Daniel asks God to turn his anger from Jerusalem

DAN.9.17-19.text: Daniel asks God to hear and forgive Israel

DAN.9.20-21.text: Gabriel comes to Daniel while Daniel prays

DAN.9.22-23.text: Gabriel has come to give Daniel understanding

DAN.9.24-25.text: Gabriel tells Daniel of seventy weeks for Jerusalem

DAN.9.26-26.text: The Messiah will be cut off and the city destroyed

DAN.9.27-27.text: A ruler makes a covenant, then stops the sacrifices

DAN.10.1-1.text: Daniel receives a true message about a great conflict

DAN.10.2-3.text: Daniel mourns and fasts for three weeks

DAN.10.4-6.text: Daniel sees a shining man by the Tigris river

DAN.10.7-9.text: Only Daniel sees the vision and loses his strength

DAN.10.10-11.text: A man touches Daniel and tells him to stand up

DAN.10.12-13.text: The angel tells Daniel his prayer was heard

DAN.10.14-15.text: The angel comes to explain the future to Daniel

DAN.10.16-17.text: Daniel is weak and cannot speak to the angel

DAN.10.18-19.text: The angel strengthens Daniel and tells him not to fear

DAN.10.20-21.text: The angel must fight the princes of Persia and Greece

DAN.11.1-2.text: The angel tells Daniel about the kings of Persia

DAN.11.3-4.text: A mighty king’s kingdom will be divided

DAN.11.5-6.text: The kings of South and North make an alliance that fails

DAN.11.7-9.text: A king from her family defeats the king of the North

DAN.11.10-10.text: The sons of the northern king gather a great army

DAN.11.11-12.text: The king of the South defeats an army but will not triumph

DAN.11.13-13.text: The king of the North raises a larger army

DAN.11.14-14.text: Many rise up against the king of the South

DAN.11.15-16.text: The king of the North captures a fortified city

DAN.11.17-19.text: The king of the North’s plans fail and he falls

DAN.11.20-22.text: A despicable man takes the kingdom in a time of peace

DAN.11.23-24.text: The king acts deceitfully and takes rich provinces

DAN.11.25-27.text: The king of the North attacks the king of the South

DAN.11.28-28.text: The king of the North returns home with great wealth

DAN.11.29-30.text: Ships of Kittim turn the king of the North back

DAN.11.31-32.text: The king’s forces desecrate the temple

DAN.11.33-35.text: The wise teach many and suffer for a time

DAN.11.36-37.text: The king exalts himself above every god

DAN.11.38-39.text: The king honors a god of fortresses

DAN.11.40-41.text: The king of the North invades many countries

DAN.11.42-43.text: The king gains power over Egypt and its riches

DAN.11.44-45.text: The king hears alarming news and meets his end

DAN.12.1-2.text: Michael rises up; Daniel’s people will be delivered

DAN.12.3-4.text: Daniel must seal the book until the end

DAN.12.5-6.text: Daniel sees two others ask the man in linen how long

DAN.12.7-7.text: The man in linen swears by God about the time

DAN.12.8-9.text: Daniel asks about the outcome, but the words are sealed

DAN.12.10-11.text: The wise will understand, but the wicked will not

DAN.12.12-13.text: Daniel will rest and receive his inheritance at the end
